newsitem.title: USA: Billy Graham to give inaugural prayer.
newsitem.headline: Billy Graham to give inaugural prayer.

text.p: Evangelist Billy Graham will take part in his eighth inauguration Monday when he gives the invocation before President Clinton and Vice President Al Gore are sworn in for their second term.
Graham, 78, gave the invocation and benediction at Clinton's first inauguration in 1993 and at President George Bush's inauguration in 1989.
He also gave a prayer at Richard Nixon's first inauguration in 1969 and preached a special worship service in the White House when Nixon began his second term in 1973.

Graham preached at inaugural day church services in Washington in 1965 when Lyndon Johnson was sworn in and in 1981 and 1985 when Ronald Reagan became president. He also attended Dwight Eisenhower's inauguration in 1953.

"I am both humbled and honoured to be invited by President Clinton to again lead the invocation at his inauguration. I have known President Clinton and Vice President Gore and their wives for many years, before they got into national office," Graham said in a statement.

Last May Graham was awarded a special Congressional Gold Medal in recognition of his 56-year career in which he has preached to more than 60 million people around the world and reached millions more through television.
